8	import {useEffect, useState} from 'react'
9	import {useVariant} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variant'
10	import {useIntl} from 'react-intl'
11	import {useVariationParams} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-params'
12	import {useVariationAttributes} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes'
13	import {useSelectedStore} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-selected-store'
14	
15	const OUT_OF_STOCK = 'OUT_OF_STOCK'
16	const UNFULFILLABLE = 'UNFULFILLABLE'
17	
18	const getInventoryById = (product, inventoryId) => {
19	    if (!inventoryId || !product?.inventories) {
20	        return null
21	    }
22	    return product.inventories.find((inv) => inv.id === inventoryId)
23	}
24	
25	// TODO: This needs to be refactored.
26	// If compatibility with API version < v8.1 is needed, keep pickupInStore as false
27	export const useDerivedProduct = (
28	    product,
29	    isProductPartOfSet = false,
30	    isProductPartOfBundle = false,
31	    pickupInStore = false,
32	    controlledVariationValues = null,
33	    onVariationChange = null
34	) => {
35	    const showLoading = !product
36	    const isProductABundle = product?.type?.bundle
37	    const stockLevel = product?.inventory?.stockLevel || 0
38	    const stepQuantity = product?.stepQuantity || 1
39	    const minOrderQuantity = stockLevel > 0 ? product?.minOrderQuantity || 1 : 0
40	    const initialQuantity = product?.quantity || product?.minOrderQuantity || 1
41	
42	    // used for product bundles when there are multiple products
43	    const lowestStockLevelProductName = product?.inventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
44	    const intl = useIntl()
45	    const variant = useVariant(
46	        product,
47	        isProductPartOfSet,
48	        isProductPartOfBundle,
49	        controlledVariationValues
50	    )
51	    const isStandardProduct = product?.type?.item
52	    const variationParams = useVariationParams(
53	        product,
54	        isProductPartOfSet,
55	        isProductPartOfBundle,
56	        controlledVariationValues
57	    )
58	    const variationAttributes = useVariationAttributes(
59	        product,
60	        isProductPartOfSet,
61	        isProductPartOfBundle,
62	        controlledVariationValues,
63	        onVariationChange
64	    )
65	    const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState(initialQuantity)
66	    const {selectedStore} = useSelectedStore()
67	
68	    // A product is considered out of stock if the stock level is 0 or if we have all our
69	    // variation attributes selected, but don't have a variant. We do this because the API
70	    // will sometimes return all the variants even if they are out of stock, but for other
71	    // products it won't.
72	    const isOutOfStock =
73	        !stockLevel ||
74	        (!isProductABundle &&
75	            !variant &&
76	            !isStandardProduct &&
77	            Object.keys(variationParams).length === variationAttributes.length) ||
78	        (!isProductABundle && variant && !variant.orderable)
79	    const unfulfillable = stockLevel < quantity
80	
81	    // Product details for selected store
82	    const selectedStoreInventory = getInventoryById(product, selectedStore?.inventoryId)
83	    const selectedStoreStockLevel = selectedStoreInventory?.stockLevel || 0
84	    const selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName =
85	        selectedStoreInventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
86	    // selectedStoreStockLevel and selectedStoreInventory are already variant specific,
87	    // so we don't need to check for variation attributes
88	    const isSelectedStoreOutOfStock = !selectedStoreStockLevel || !selectedStoreInventory?.orderable
89	    const selectedStoreUnfulfillable = selectedStoreStockLevel < quantity
90	
91	    // Use appropriate inventory based on pickup/delivery selection
92	    const currentStockLevel = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreStockLevel : stockLevel
93	    const currentLowestStockLevelProductName = pickupInStore
94	        ? selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName
95	        : lowestStockLevelProductName
96	    const currentIsOutOfStock = pickupInStore ? isSelectedStoreOutOfStock : isOutOfStock
97	    const currentUnfulfillable = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreUnfulfillable : unfulfillable
98	
99	    const inventoryMessages = {
100	        [OUT_OF_STOCK]: intl.formatMessage({
101	            defaultMessage: 'Out of stock',
102	            id: 'use_product.message.out_of_stock'
103	        }),
104	        [UNFULFILLABLE]: currentLowestStockLevelProductName
105	            ? intl.formatMessage(
106	                  {
107	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left for {productName}!',
108	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining_for_product'
109	                  },
110	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel, productName: currentLowestStockLevelProductName}
111	              )
112	            : intl.formatMessage(
113	                  {
114	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left!',
115	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining'
116	                  },
117	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel}
118	              )
119	    }
120	
121	    // showInventoryMessage controls if add to cart button is disabled
122	    const showInventoryMessage =
123	        (variant || isProductABundle || isStandardProduct) &&
124	        (currentIsOutOfStock || currentUnfulfillable)
125	    const inventoryMessage =
126	        (currentIsOutOfStock && inventoryMessages[OUT_OF_STOCK]) ||
127	        (currentUnfulfillable && inventoryMessages[UNFULFILLABLE])
128	
129	    // If the `initialQuantity` changes, update the state. This typically happens
130	    // when either the master product changes, or the inventory of the product changes
131	    // from out-of-stock to in-stock or vice versa.
132	    useEffect(() => {
133	        setQuantity(initialQuantity)
134	    }, [initialQuantity])
135	
136	    // Lump the out of stock/unfulfillable checks together for easier consumption
137	    return {
138	        showLoading,
139	        showInventoryMessage,
140	        inventoryMessage,
141	        variationAttributes,
142	        quantity,
143	        minOrderQuantity,
144	        stepQuantity,
145	        variationParams,
146	        setQuantity,
147	        variant,
148	        stockLevel,
149	        isOutOfStock,
150	        unfulfillable,
151	        isSelectedStoreOutOfStock: isSelectedStoreOutOfStock || selectedStoreUnfulfillable,
152	        selectedStore
153	    }
154	}

27	import React from 'react';
28	import {
29	  AspectRatio,
30	  Box,
31	  Badge,
32	  Image,
33	  useMultiStyleConfig,
34	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
35	import { useItemVariant } from '.';
36	import { FormattedMessage } from 'react-intl';
37	import { findImageGroupBy } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils';
38	// Recipe key — single source in item-variant.css.ts (SFCC-270 round 2 rework), no longer
39	// redeclared per file.
40	import { ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE } from './item-variant.css';
41	
42	// See index.tsx's own note on why this is `any` rather than a structural type.
43	type SfccVariant = any;
44	
45	type ItemImageProps = {
46	  imageProps?: Record<string, any>;
47	  ratio?: number;
48	} & Record<string, any>;
49	
50	// Figma "Image" spec, product-item card (SFCC-270): aspect ratio 288/432, which reduces to 2/3
51	// exactly. Matches the design record's own 132x198 desktop pair exactly (132 * 432/288 = 198);
52	// against the 67x100 mobile pair it lands at 100.5 — half a pixel over the stated 100, the same
53	// class of Figma-rounding gap zimmDrawer.css.ts's WIDTH_XLARGE note already documents for a
54	// different value, not something introduced here.
55	const CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO = 288 / 432;
56	
57	/**
58	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
59	 * main image.
60	 *
61	 * @todo = This component will render a `SALE` badge when the qualifier is available
62	 * on the custom property `c_isSale`. This will need to be expanded upon to handle
63	 * different badge/qualifiers and property names.
64	 */
65	const ItemImage = ({ imageProps, ratio = CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO, ...props }: ItemImageProps) => {
66	  const variant: SfccVariant = useItemVariant();
67	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE, {});
68	
69	  // We find the 'small' images in the variant's image groups based on variationValues and pick the first one
70	  const image = findImageGroupBy(variant?.imageGroups, {
71	    viewType: 'small',
72	    selectedVariationAttributes: variant?.variationValues,
73	  })?.images?.[0];
74	
75	  return (
76	    <Box __css={styles.image} {...props}>
77	      <AspectRatio ratio={ratio}>
78	        <Box position="relative">
79	          {variant.c_isSale && (
80	            <Badge
81	              position="absolute"
82	              top={0}
83	              left={0}
84	              marginLeft={2}
85	              marginTop={2}
86	              fontSize="10px"
87	              variant="solid"
88	              colorScheme="blue"
89	            >
90	              <FormattedMessage
91	                defaultMessage="Sale"
92	                id="item_image.label.sale"
93	                description="A sale badge placed on top of a product image"
94	              />
95	            </Badge>
96	          )}
97	          {variant.isProductUnavailable && (
98	            <Badge
99	              position="absolute"
100	              top={0}
101	              left={0}
102	              marginLeft={2}
103	              marginTop={2}
104	              fontSize="10px"
105	              variant="solid"
106	              colorScheme="red"
107	            >
108	              <FormattedMessage
109	                defaultMessage="Unavailable"
110	                id="item_image.label.unavailable"
111	                description="A unavailable badge placed on top of a product image"
112	              />
113	            </Badge>
114	          )}
115	
116	          {image && (
117	            <Image
118	              alt={image.alt}
119	              src={`${image.disBaseLink || image.link}`}
120	              ignoreFallback={true}
121	              __css={styles.img}
122	              {...imageProps}
123	            />
124	          )}
125	        </Box>
126	      </AspectRatio>
127	    </Box>
128	  );
129	};
130	
131	export default ItemImage;

/*
 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-name.jsx
 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step beyond the TypeScript annotation and a
 * temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed).
 *
 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
 * `Link` is not overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing at time of
 * writing), so it stays on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path.
 *
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2), bug fix: base had `<Link {...props} color="black.600" to={...}>` —
 * spreading `props` BEFORE the explicit `color`/`to`, the opposite order from item-image/
 * item-attributes/item-price's own `{...props}` placement (spread last), so a caller-supplied
 * `color` was silently overridden here instead of taking precedence, unlike those three
 * siblings. Fixed by moving `color` ahead of the spread, matching the siblings' order — `to`
 * stays after the spread, unchanged, since it is data-derived (from `productId`) and was never
 * meant to be caller-overridable the way `color` is. No current base caller passes `color`, so
 * nothing observable changes for them; this only matters going forward.
 *
 * Also restyled per the Figma cart-item spec: `fontSize="md"` (a bare Chakra token — this
 * repo's own `fontSizes` scale is deliberately NOT registered as `theme.fontSizes`, see
 * typography.ts, so that literal was silently reading Chakra's own unrelated default) replaced
 * by `textStyle="productNames"`, which also carries the spec's "uppercase" requirement (see
 * typography.ts's `productNames` entry). The bug-fixed default colour is expressed as a literal
 * `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` prop rather than routed through the recipe: a plain literal
 * prop is provably override-safe here regardless of `Link`'s own internal implementation (it
 * lands in the same `props` bucket a caller's own `color` would use), where `__css`/`sx` on this
 * specific base `Link` wrapper is not — see item-variant.css.ts's own docblock for the
 * `__css`-discarding hazard that rules `__css` out for a plain Chakra `Text`, a nearby but
 * distinct case worth being equally careful about here.
 */
import React from 'react';
import { useItemVariant } from '.';
import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
import { Heading } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

/**
 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this components simply renders
 * the item's name using the cart item field `productName`. We use this field
 * rather than variant `name` field as the variant detail may not yet be
 * available upon rendering.
 */
const ItemName = (props: Record<string, any>) => {
  const variant = useItemVariant();
  const productId = variant?.master?.masterId || variant.id;

  return (
    <Heading as="h2" textStyle="productNames">
      <Link color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" {...props} to={`/product/${productId}`}>
        {variant.productName || variant.name}
      </Link>
    </Heading>
  );
};

export default ItemName;

1	/**
2	 * Allow-list guard for hrefs that originate outside the codebase.
3	 *
4	 * Anything reaching an `href` from Contentful, a URL parameter, or a prop supplied by a
5	 * caller we do not control has to pass through here first. `javascript:` and `data:` URLs
6	 * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
7	 * lookahead rejects that, including the backslash form — a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`,
8	 * so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as a second slash is. `e9c2180` closed
9	 * only the forward-slash half; the backslash and control-character forms stayed open until now.
10	 *
11	 * Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a deny-list has to anticipate every scheme,
12	 * and browsers keep adding them.
13	 */
14	// eslint-disable no-control-regex — the control characters ARE the subject here. The rule exists
15	// to catch them appearing by accident; these are deliberate, and matching them is the whole point
16	// of the fix. Suppressed at the point of use rather than in .eslintrc, per the escape-hatch
17	// convention in .claude/rules/typescript.md.
18	/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
19	const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
20	const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
21	/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
22	
23	/**
24	 * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
25	 *
26	 * The WHATWG parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
27	 * in the input, BEFORE it parses. `/\u0009/evil.com` is therefore parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing
28	 * the raw string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves — which
29	 * is exactly how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open.
30	 *
31	 * A plain space is deliberately not stripped: the parser percent-encodes it rather than removing
32	 * it, so `/ /evil.com` resolves on-site and must stay allowed.
33	 */
34	const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
35	
36	const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
37	
38	/** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
39	export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false);
40	
41	/**
42	 * A single leading `/` is a same-origin relative path that needs the current site/locale prefix
43	 * from `useMultiSite()`'s `buildUrl()` (see `buildSafeHref`/`useSafeHref`) before it's safe to
44	 * navigate to — an unprefixed internal path always falls back to the default site.
45	 *
46	 * Checks the normalised value, same as `isSafeHref` — a raw, un-normalised check would disagree
47	 * with `isSafeHref` on a value like a leading-space href (`normalise` strips it, `isSafeHref`
48	 * allows it), misclassifying a real internal path as external and silently skipping `buildUrl`.
49	 *
50	 * Relies on `isSafeHref` having already run: that regex's own negative lookahead is what keeps
51	 * `//host`/`/\host` (off-site authority references) out of this function's input in practice, so
52	 * this check only needs to distinguish "internal path" from the other forms `isSafeHref` allows
53	 * (`https?:`, `tel:`, `mailto:`, `#fragment`) — every one of which must NOT be run through
54	 * `buildUrl` (it would corrupt an absolute/external URL, or replace an in-page fragment's own
55	 * page path with just the site prefix).
56	 */
57	export const isInternalHref = (href: string): boolean => normalise(href).startsWith('/');
58	
59	/**
60	 * Runs `href` through `buildUrl()` only when it's an internal path (see `isInternalHref`) —
61	 * every other form `isSafeHref` allows is returned unchanged, exactly as given (not normalised —
62	 * normalising an external/tel/mailto/# value isn't this function's job). `buildUrl` itself
63	 * receives the *normalised* internal path, not the raw one, so a leading-space href doesn't leak
64	 * a stray character into the prefixed URL. `buildUrl` is passed in rather than looked up here
65	 * since this module has no hook of its own; see `useSafeHref`
66	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useSafeHref.ts`) for the hook form of this same composition, and for the
67	 * single place every internal-navigation call site in this app should reach for.
68	 */
69	export const buildSafeHref = (href: string, buildUrl: (path: string) => string): string => {
70	  const normalisedHref = normalise(href);
71	  return isInternalHref(normalisedHref) ? buildUrl(normalisedHref) : href;
72	};

import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';

/**
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute — a real BM site preference
 * (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto the SCAPI product response via a
 * `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046). It has no
 * typed field on the base SDK's `Product` type — it only reaches this shape via that type's own
 * `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, the same situation
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` lines 16-23 document for a
 * different custom attribute (`c_productBadges`). Narrowed here to a local type rather than
 * trusting `any` at the call site, per AGENTS.md's Gotchas: "Commerce SDK types not importable
 * ... declare a narrow local type."
 *
 * Typed `unknown`, not `number | undefined`: this function's whole job is validating a value
 * that may legitimately arrive absent, as `0`, negative, or non-numeric (see the pass criteria
 * this file's own test covers) — typing it as `number | undefined` would assert a guarantee the
 * real BM data doesn't have.
 *
 * As of this commit `TSD-SFCC-268` is still `v0.1 Draft` (Technical Lead sign-off Pending) and a
 * live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is
 * not deployed yet. Reading the field with the fallback below degrades to today's hardcoded
 * behaviour while that remains true, and picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships,
 * with no further frontend change needed.
 */
type ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
  c_maxOrderQuantity?: unknown;
};

/**
 * Frontend fallback when no valid `c_maxOrderQuantity` is present. Matches
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
 */
const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;

/**
 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
 *
 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
 * valid value is present.
 */
export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
};

 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
 */
const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;

/**
 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
 *
 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
 * valid value is present.
 */
export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
};

14	 * @param {Object} options.selectedVariationAttributes - A key/value object consisting of attibute id's and their values.
15	 * @returns {Object} - The ImageGroup matching the search criteria

17	export const findImageGroupBy = (imageGroups = [], options) => {
18	    let {viewType, selectedVariationAttributes = {}} = options
19	
20	    // Start by filtering out any imageGroup that isn't the correct viewType.
21	    imageGroups = imageGroups.filter(
22	        ({viewType: imageGroupViewType}) => imageGroupViewType === viewType
23	    )
24	
25	    // Not all variation attributes are reflected in images. For example, you probably
26	    // won't have a separate image group for various sizes, but you might for colors. For that
27	    // reason we need to know what are valid attribute values to filter on.
28	    const refinableAttributeIds = [
29	        ...new Set(
30	            imageGroups
31	                .reduce((acc, {variationAttributes = []}) => [...acc, ...variationAttributes], [])
32	                .map(({id}) => id)
33	        )
34	    ]
35	
36	    // Update the `selectedVariationAttributes` by filtering out the attributes that have no
37	    // representation in this imageGroup.
38	    selectedVariationAttributes = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes).reduce((acc, curr) => {
39	        return refinableAttributeIds.includes(curr)
40	            ? {
41	                  ...acc,
42	                  [`${curr}`]: selectedVariationAttributes[curr]
43	              }
44	            : acc
45	    }, {})
46	
47	    // Find the image group that has all the all the selected variation value attributes.
48	    imageGroups = imageGroups.find(({variationAttributes = []}) => {
49	        const selectedIds = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes)
50	
51	        return selectedIds.every((selectedId) => {
52	            const selectedValue = selectedVariationAttributes[selectedId]
53	
54	            return variationAttributes.find(
55	                ({id, values}) =>
56	                    id === selectedId && values.every(({value}) => value === selectedValue)
57	            )
58	        })
59	    })

5	/*
6	 * Converts an SDK basket `productItem` into a self-contained display-data shape, mirroring the
7	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` precedent (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`,
8	 * PR #85) for how a page-scoped SDK-to-props mapper is organised in this codebase: a single
9	 * exported "select" function, an untyped-base-package input narrowed to a local type, and a
10	 * `.test.ts` asserting the mapped shape directly (see that file's own `ProductListSearchHit`/
11	 * `RawImage` pattern, mirrored below for `CartLineItem`/`CartItemImage`).
12	 *
13	 * Disclosed design choice, not a directly sourced requirement (flagged per this step's own
14	 * instructions): `ProductItem`/`ItemVariantProvider` (`overrides/app/components/product-item/
15	 * index.tsx:140`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/index.tsx:43`) both currently declare
16	 * their real data-carrying prop as the raw untyped basket/product object itself
17	 * (`product`/`variant`, both `SfccProduct`/`SfccVariant = any`) — today's leaves read every
18	 * display field (image, name, combined attributes) directly off that object via
19	 * `useItemVariant()`, not from individually-mapped props. This mapper is, per this step's plan
20	 * text, "an as-yet-unused-by-anything-else container-layer function" — it does not change or
21	 * feed either of those two files (out of this step's scope). What it produces instead is a pure,
22	 * tested equivalent of the specific per-field computations those leaves and
23	 * `product-quantity-picker.tsx`/`use-derived-product.js` already perform internally off that same
24	 * raw object (image+alt, combined colour/size, quantity, stepQuantity) — ready for whichever
25	 * future step decides how a real page hands data down, without having modified any of those
26	 * existing files.
27	 *
28	 * `CartLineItem` models the REAL runtime shape a basket line item has by the time it reaches
29	 * those leaves: the un-overridden base cart page never passes the raw `basket.productItems[i]`
30	 * alone — it merges it with the matching full `Product` (fetched separately via `useProducts`)
31	 * before handing it down: `product={{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[productItem.itemId],
32	 * price: productItem.price, quantity: ...}}` (see

34	 * `<ProductItem product={...}>` call). `imageGroups`/`variationAttributes`/`variationValues`/
35	 * `stepQuantity`/`name` all come from that merged-in `Product` half, not from
36	 * `ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` itself (confirmed against its generated fields — it has no
37	 * image/variation/stepQuantity fields at all beyond its own `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all).
38	 */

import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';

/**
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute — a real BM site preference
 * (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto the SCAPI product response via a
 * `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046). It has no
 * typed field on the base SDK's `Product` type — it only reaches this shape via that type's own
 * `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, the same situation
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` lines 16-23 document for a
 * different custom attribute (`c_productBadges`). Narrowed here to a local type rather than
 * trusting `any` at the call site, per AGENTS.md's Gotchas: "Commerce SDK types not importable
 * ... declare a narrow local type."
 *
 * Typed `unknown`, not `number | undefined`: this function's whole job is validating a value
 * that may legitimately arrive absent, as `0`, negative, or non-numeric (see the pass criteria
 * this file's own test covers) — typing it as `number | undefined` would assert a guarantee the
 * real BM data doesn't have.
 *
 * As of this commit `TSD-SFCC-268` is still `v0.1 Draft` (Technical Lead sign-off Pending) and a
 * live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is
 * not deployed yet. Reading the field with the fallback below degrades to today's hardcoded
 * behaviour while that remains true, and picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships,
 * with no further frontend change needed.
 */
type ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
  c_maxOrderQuantity?: unknown;
};

/**
 * Frontend fallback when no valid `c_maxOrderQuantity` is present. Matches
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
 */
const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;

/**
 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
 *
 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
 * valid value is present.
 */
export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
};

## Branch check
`git branch --show-current` → `feature/SFCC-11_cart`. Not `develop`/`main`. Proceeded.

## Files created (nothing else touched — `git status --porcelain` shows exactly these 3 paths, no modified files)

1. **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`** — exports `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)`. Reads `c_maxOrderQuantity` off a `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`-shaped object; returns it only when it's a finite number `> 0`, otherwise falls back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3` (its own constant, independent from `product-detail/index.tsx`'s `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY`).
2. **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.test.ts`** — 5 tests.
3. **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartItemMapper.ts`** (new folder) — exports `selectCartItemProps(item)`, a pure function mapping a merged basket-line-item shape to `{itemId, productId, name, image: {src, alt}, combinedAttributes, quantity, stepQuantity}`. No hooks, no React.
4. **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartItemMapper.test.ts`** — 4 tests.

No Storybook stories — correctly: neither file is a component (components.md's story rule targets components, not pure utilities), so a `.test.ts` is the right and complete coverage per testing.md.

## Pass criteria — evidence

**1. `maxOrderQuantity.test.ts` (5 tests, all passing):** present+valid → returns it; absent → 3; `0` → 3; negative → 3; non-numeric (a string `'5'`, chosen because a misconfigured BM attribute could realistically arrive as a string) → 3.

**2. `cartItemMapper.test.ts` (4 tests, all passing):** full line item → asserts the complete mapped object via `toEqual`; missing `imageGroups` → asserts `image.src` is `undefined` and `image.alt` is the defined, non-empty `productName` fallback (no throw); colour+size → asserts `combinedAttributes === 'Lilac Sand, One size'`, the exact example already cited in `item-attributes.tsx:31`; quantity/stepQuantity → asserts both pass through unchanged (`3`/`2`, values chosen specifically to not collide with the `1` fallback, so the test actually proves passthrough rather than accidentally hitting the fallback path).

**3. Grep check — run literally, does NOT return nothing.** See "what Marcel is missing" below — this is pre-existing, not caused by this step.

**4. No new `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3`; `product-detail/index.tsx` untouched.** `grep -rn "MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY" overrides/` shows only the pre-existing declaration/usage at `product-detail/index.tsx:125,1294` plus my own comment *citing* that name in a docblock (not a declaration). `git status --porcelain` confirms zero modified files, only 3 new untracked paths.

## Verification run
`npx tsc --noEmit` → clean, exit 0 (twice — before and after a citation-accuracy fix, see below).
`npm run test` → **95 files, 1320 tests, all passing**, including `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6 tests, unaffected — neither new file has any styling/JSX, so the styling gate doesn't apply to them at all; `npm run audit:tokens` is likewise inapplicable for the same reason). Re-ran only the two new files + `recipeGuards.test.ts` after a docblock-wording fix (comment-only, couldn't affect behaviour) rather than the full suite a second time.

## Judgement calls (flagged, not silently decided)

1. **The exact shape `cartItemMapper` targets.** `ProductItem`/`ItemVariantProvider` (`product-item/index.tsx:140`, `item-variant/index.tsx:43`) both currently declare their real data-carrying prop as the *raw* object itself (`product`/`variant`, both typed `any`) — today's leaves pull every field off it via `useItemVariant()`, not from individually-mapped props. Since the plan calls this mapper "as-yet-unused-by-anything-else," I designed its output as a self-contained shape mirroring exactly the per-field computations those leaves + `product-quantity-picker.tsx`/`use-derived-product.js` already do internally (image+alt, combined attributes, quantity, stepQuantity) — not a literal `ProductItemProps`, since that type doesn't have individual fields to map to. Documented at length in the file's own module docblock, citing the base `product-item-list/index.jsx`'s real merge logic (`product={{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[itemId], ...}}`) as evidence for why `CartLineItem` intersects `ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` with a `Pick` of `Product` fields (imageGroups/variationAttributes/variationValues/stepQuantity/name never appear on the typed basket `ProductItem` itself — verified against its generated fields).
2. **Missing-image alt fallback:** `image?.alt || item.productName || item.name || ''` — guarantees a defined, non-empty alt whenever a name is available, going one step further than `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `toCardImage` (which returns `undefined` for the whole image, no alt at all, on a miss) — justified because a PLP card can skip rendering on no image, a cart line item cannot.
3. **Combined colour+size order is inherited, not re-sorted.** I reused `getDisplayVariationValues` + `Object.values(...).join(', ')` verbatim (the same two-step call `item-attributes.tsx:98,148-150` already uses) rather than writing new logic to force colour-first ordering. The order comes from whatever order the input `variationValues` object's own keys are in — same assumption the existing, already-shipped component already carries. My test data is deliberately ordered `{color, size}` to demonstrate this produces the documented order for realistic data, not to prove it's independently guaranteed.
4. **`stepQuantity` gets a fallback (`|| 1`), `quantity`/`itemId`/`productId` do not.** The plan says "quantity and stepQuantity passed through" — I read `stepQuantity`'s fallback as inherited from an existing, real precedent (`use-derived-product.js:38`'s own `product?.stepQuantity || 1`) rather than invented, while `quantity` has no such precedent, so it's a pure, unmodified passthrough.

## A pre-existing condition this step's own pass criterion surfaced (not caused by this step)

Pass criterion 3's grep, run exactly as specified, does **not** return nothing:
```
overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx:45:import { useCurrentBasket } from '.../use-current-basket';
overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx:46:import { usePromotions, useProducts, useProduct } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx:78,102,128: real calls to all three
```
This is real, already-shipped application code (SFCC-270, promotions-popover and bundle-child data fetching) — not a test/mock artifact, and not touched by this step (confirmed via `git status`; neither of my two new files imports any commerce-sdk-react hook). It directly contradicts the "prop-driven leaf, no data-fetching hook" invariant this pass criterion exists to check. My own two files are clean of this pattern. Whether this is a known/accepted exception, or a genuine drift worth a separate ticket, is Marcel's call — I did not touch `item-attributes.tsx` (out of scope, and it's a shared component other squads/tests depend on).

## Unverified gaps (mine)
- No independent live-API check that a real Zimmermann basket line item's `variationValues` really arrives ordered `{color, size}` — I relied entirely on the existing, already-shipped docblock citation (`item-attributes.tsx:31`) claiming this for real catalog data, not a fresh check of my own.
- `Pick<ShopperProductsTypes.Product, ...>`'s resulting field types compile clean, but I did not independently confirm (e.g. via IDE hover) whether TS resolves them to the narrow array types or collapses to `any` given `Product`'s own `{[key:string]: any}` catch-all — either way is harmless (nothing consumes these types downstream yet) and `tsc --noEmit` is clean regardless.
- `getMaxOrderQuantity`'s real end-to-end behaviour against a live `c_maxOrderQuantity` value is unprovable until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook actually deploys (confirmed absent on dev sandbox per this build's own `findings.md` #2) — inherited limitation, not something this step can close.

## What Marcel is missing

Two earlier planning artifacts for this same build describe a **different, simpler** design than what this step's actual plan text (and pass criteria) asked for: `findings.md` line 107 says the resolution is "a shared helper," and `HANDOFF.md` line 56 shorthands it as `product?.c_maxOrderQuantity ?? MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` (plain `??`, which would let `0`/negative through uncaught — the opposite of pass criterion 1). I followed the actual, more detailed step-3.4 text and its pass criteria (independent constant, full positive-number validation) since that's what governs this step and is internally well-reasoned — but both older documents are now stale on this specific point and could mislead a future reader who checks them instead of the plan.

Separately: the item-attributes.tsx finding above is worth a look independent of this step — it's a real, live violation of an architectural invariant the whole B3 arc (and this step's pass criterion 3) is built on, sitting in a shared file three other component folders' tests already have to mock around.
